137	#### Lifts of subalgebras of setoid algebras
138	
139	Ten lemmas of one shape: transport a `≤` or a `≥` across the isomorphism between
140	an algebra and its lift.  The seven one-sided ones are each a single application
141	of a mixed transitivity lemma from above to one of the `Lift-≅`{.AgdaFunction}
142	isomorphisms of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Isomorphisms][]; the three
143	`Lift-≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} variants then compose two of those.  Either way no
144	lemma is more than a line, which is the concrete sense in which universe lifting
145	costs nothing here.
146	
147	The suffix says which level moves, following `Lift-Algˡ`{.AgdaFunction},
148	`Lift-Algʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and `Lift-Alg`{.AgdaFunction} of
149	[Setoid.Algebras.Basic][]: `ˡ` raises the level of the carrier, `ʳ` the level of
150	the equality, and the unadorned name raises both.
151	
152	+  `≤-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `≤-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
153	   `≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} lift the algebra on the right of `≤`, the larger one;
154	+  `≥-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `≥-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
155	   `≥-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} do the same for `≥`, which lifts the smaller one;
156	+  `Lift-≤-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `Lift-≤-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
157	   `Lift-≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} lift both algebras at once, and are literally the
158	   composition of the two groups above;
159	+  `Lift-is-sub`{.AgdaFunction} is the class-relative version: lifting an algebra
160	   does not disturb its being a subalgebra of some member of `𝒦`.

164	  {𝒦 : Pred (Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ)(ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} α)}
165	  {𝑩 : Algebra β ρᵇ} {ℓ : Level}
166	  → 𝑩 ≤c 𝒦 → (Lift-Algˡ 𝑩 ℓ) ≤c 𝒦
167	Lift-is-sub (𝑨 , (KA , B≤A)) = 𝑨 , (KA , A≥B×B≅C→A≥C B≤A Lift-≅ˡ)
168	
169	module _ {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} where
170	  ≤-Liftˡ : {ℓ : Level} → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≤ Lift-Algˡ 𝑩 ℓ
171	  ≤-Liftˡ A≤B = A≤B×B≅C→A≤C A≤B Lift-≅ˡ
172	
173	  ≤-Liftʳ : {ρ : Level} → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≤ Lift-Algʳ 𝑩 ρ
174	  ≤-Liftʳ A≤B = A≤B×B≅C→A≤C A≤B Lift-≅ʳ
175	
176	  ≤-Lift : {ℓ ρ : Level} → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≤ Lift-Alg 𝑩 ℓ ρ
177	  ≤-Lift A≤B = A≤B×B≅C→A≤C  A≤B Lift-≅
178	
179	  ≥-Liftˡ : {ℓ : Level} → 𝑨 ≥ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≥ Lift-Algˡ 𝑩 ℓ
180	  ≥-Liftˡ A≥B = A≥B×B≅C→A≥C A≥B Lift-≅ˡ

183	  ≥-Liftʳ A≥B = A≥B×B≅C→A≥C A≥B Lift-≅ʳ
184	
185	  ≥-Lift : {ℓ ρ : Level} → 𝑨 ≥ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≥ Lift-Alg 𝑩 ℓ ρ
186	  ≥-Lift A≥B = A≥B×B≅C→A≥C A≥B Lift-≅
187	
188	module _ {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} where
189	  Lift-≤-Liftˡ : {ℓᵃ ℓᵇ : Level} → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩 → Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 ℓᵃ ≤ Lift-Algˡ 𝑩 ℓᵇ
190	  Lift-≤-Liftˡ A≤B = ≥-Liftˡ (≤-Liftˡ A≤B)
191	
192	  Lift-≤-Liftʳ : {rᵃ rᵇ : Level} → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩 → Lift-Algʳ 𝑨 rᵃ ≤ Lift-Algʳ 𝑩 rᵇ
193	  Lift-≤-Liftʳ A≤B = ≥-Liftʳ (≤-Liftʳ A≤B)
194	
195	  Lift-≤-Lift : {a rᵃ b rᵇ : Level}
196	    → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩 → Lift-Alg 𝑨 a rᵃ ≤ Lift-Alg 𝑩 b rᵇ
197	  Lift-≤-Lift A≤B = ≥-Lift (≤-Lift A≤B)
198	```
199	
200	#### Products of subalgebras
201	
202	`⨅-≤`{.AgdaFunction} is the compatibility of the subalgebra relation with
203	products: if `ℬ i ≤ 𝒜 i` for every index `i`, then `⨅ ℬ ≤ ⨅ 𝒜`.  The embedding is
204	assembled coordinatewise from the given ones, and injectivity is coordinatewise
205	too, because two elements of a product are equal exactly when they agree in every
206	coordinate.
207	
208	Small as it is, this is the load-bearing step of `PS⊆SP`{.AgdaFunction} in
209	[Setoid.Varieties.Preservation][], where a product of subalgebras has to be
210	recognised as a subalgebra of a product so that `S`{.AgdaFunction} and
211	`P`{.AgdaFunction} can be interchanged.
212	
213	```agda
214	module _
215	  {I : Type ι}
216	  {𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}
217	  {ℬ : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}
218	  where
219	  open IsHom
220	
221	  ⨅-≤ : (∀ i → ℬ i ≤ 𝒜 i) → ⨅ ℬ ≤ ⨅ 𝒜
222	  ⨅-≤ B≤A = h , hM
223	    where
224	    h : hom (⨅ ℬ) (⨅ 𝒜)
225	    h = hfunc , hhom
226	      where
227	      homAt : ∀ i → hom (ℬ i) (𝒜 i)
228	      homAt = λ i → proj₁ (B≤A i)
229	
230	      hmapAt : ∀ i → 𝔻[ ℬ i ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝒜 i ]
231	      hmapAt = proj₁ ∘ homAt
232	
233	      hfunc : 𝔻[ ⨅ ℬ ] ⟶ 𝔻[ ⨅ 𝒜 ]
234	      hfunc ⟨$⟩ x = λ i → (hmapAt i) ⟨$⟩ (x i)
235	      hfunc .cong = λ xy i → cong (hmapAt i) (xy i)
236	
237	      hhom : IsHom (⨅ ℬ) (⨅ 𝒜) hfunc
238	      hhom .compatible = λ i → compatible (proj₂ (homAt i))
239	
240	    hM : IsInjective (proj₁ h)
241	    hM = λ xy i → (proj₂ (B≤A i)) (xy i)
242	```

#### Properties of the subalgebra relation for setoid algebras

This is the [Setoid.Subalgebras.Properties][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

This module establishes the order-theoretic facts about the subalgebra relation
`_≤_`{.AgdaFunction} that the rest of the library relies on: that it is a
preorder, that isomorphism refines it in either direction, that it survives
universe lifting, and that it is preserved by products.

The preorder is stated with respect to isomorphism rather than equality
(`≤-preorder`{.AgdaFunction}), which is the only sensible choice, since mutual
embeddings do not make two algebras equal.  The universe-lifting group is the
part used most often, for the reason recorded in [Setoid.Algebras.Basic][]:
Agda's universes are not cumulative, so a `≤` established at one level has to be
transported explicitly before it can be used at another.

<!--

The subalgebra relation is a *preorder*, i.e., a reflexive, transitive binary relation.

```agda
open _≅_

≅→≤ : {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} → 𝑨 ≅ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑩
≅→≤ φ = (to φ) , ≅toInjective φ

≅→≥ : {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} → 𝑨 ≅ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≥ 𝑩

≤-refl = ≅→≤

≥-refl : {𝑨 𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ} → 𝑨 ≅ 𝑩 → 𝑨 ≥ 𝑩
≥-refl = ≅→≤ ∘ ≅-sym

≤-reflexive : {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ} → 𝑨 ≤ 𝑨
≤-reflexive {𝑨 = 𝑨} = 𝒾𝒹 , id-is-injective {𝑨 = 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]}

module _ {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}{𝑪 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} γ ρᶜ} where
```

#### Lifts of subalgebras of setoid algebras

Ten lemmas of one shape: transport a `≤` or a `≥` across the isomorphism between
an algebra and its lift.  The seven one-sided ones are each a single application
of a mixed transitivity lemma from above to one of the `Lift-≅`{.AgdaFunction}
isomorphisms of [Setoid.Homomorphisms.Isomorphisms][]; the three
`Lift-≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} variants then compose two of those.  Either way no
lemma is more than a line, which is the concrete sense in which universe lifting
costs nothing here.

The suffix says which level moves, following `Lift-Algˡ`{.AgdaFunction},
`Lift-Algʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and `Lift-Alg`{.AgdaFunction} of
[Setoid.Algebras.Basic][]: `ˡ` raises the level of the carrier, `ʳ` the level of
the equality, and the unadorned name raises both.

+  `≤-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `≤-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
   `≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} lift the algebra on the right of `≤`, the larger one;
+  `≥-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `≥-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
   `≥-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} do the same for `≥`, which lifts the smaller one;
+  `Lift-≤-Liftˡ`{.AgdaFunction}, `Lift-≤-Liftʳ`{.AgdaFunction} and
   `Lift-≤-Lift`{.AgdaFunction} lift both algebras at once, and are literally the

#### Products of subalgebras

`⨅-≤`{.AgdaFunction} is the compatibility of the subalgebra relation with
products: if `ℬ i ≤ 𝒜 i` for every index `i`, then `⨅ ℬ ≤ ⨅ 𝒜`.  The embedding is
assembled coordinatewise from the given ones, and injectivity is coordinatewise
too, because two elements of a product are equal exactly when they agree in every
coordinate.

Small as it is, this is the load-bearing step of `PS⊆SP`{.AgdaFunction} in
[Setoid.Varieties.Preservation][], where a product of subalgebras has to be
recognised as a subalgebra of a product so that `S`{.AgdaFunction} and
`P`{.AgdaFunction} can be interchanged.

```agda
module _
  {I : Type ι}
  {𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}
  {ℬ : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}
  where
  open IsHom

  ⨅-≤ : (∀ i → ℬ i ≤ 𝒜 i) → ⨅ ℬ ≤ ⨅ 𝒜
  ⨅-≤ B≤A = h , hM
    where
    h : hom (⨅ ℬ) (⨅ 𝒜)
    h = hfunc , hhom
      where
      homAt : ∀ i → hom (ℬ i) (𝒜 i)
      homAt = λ i → proj₁ (B≤A i)

      hmapAt : ∀ i → 𝔻[ ℬ i ] ⟶ 𝔻[ 𝒜 i ]
      hmapAt = proj₁ ∘ homAt

      hfunc : 𝔻[ ⨅ ℬ ] ⟶ 𝔻[ ⨅ 𝒜 ]
      hfunc ⟨$⟩ x = λ i → (hmapAt i) ⟨$⟩ (x i)
      hfunc .cong = λ xy i → cong (hmapAt i) (xy i)

      hhom : IsHom (⨅ ℬ) (⨅ 𝒜) hfunc
      hhom .compatible = λ i → compatible (proj₂ (homAt i))

    hM : IsInjective (proj₁ h)
    hM = λ xy i → (proj₂ (B≤A i)) (xy i)
```
